label: final copy step of length-3 sequences (weak, token-dependent)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase on a repeated input (in_first=0), at recall_idx>=2; never in the original phase or at the delimiter. The strongest activations (top quartile ~68% covered) are at the last step (t=5) of L=3 sequences, where the model outputs orig(2) after copying orig(1); about 7% of L=3 sequences fire here, 54% of activation mass. Within that, magnitude is token-dependent: inputs c, m, d, v, 3 give the largest values (top examples nearly all have orig(1)=c); restricting to these raises precision to ~0.71 but drops recall. The remaining ~46% of mass is weaker, scattered over mid-copy steps (t=11-13) of L=7-9 sequences, again preferring input c or m, with no clean rule. Does not fire on first occurrences of a token, on original-phase steps, or at recall_idx 0-1. The predicate covers only the L=3 component and is imprecise.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the previous input (most: s, 1, x, t, z, w; least: 2, k, r, h) and the current input token, by step (t=12: c, m, a, x; t=11: c, m, x, d; t=10: c, m, p, a); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=5, L=3, L=4 & t=6.
